title: flaky: two default-timeout tests red `pnpm test` under full-repo parallelism — `types/src/node.test.ts` (5s) and `dogfood/test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts` (10s hookTimeout)
body:
Found while taking the machine-lane baseline for the QA wave (#9296, round #9298). Filed as a finding, not fixed — R0 does not land code.

Same defect class as the already-closed precedents #3662, #4186, #4485, #5421, #6329: a test on a **default vitest timeout** that only passes when it is not competing for CPU. Two more instances, neither previously filed.

## What failed

### 1. `@objectstack/types` — `src/node.test.ts`

```
FAIL src/node.test.ts > host-app package resolution (cloud#1013, #4700)
     > falls back to the importing package's own resolution when the host does not declare
Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
 ❯ src/node.test.ts:178:3
```

Reported as `15 tests | 1 failed`, the failing case taking **5061 ms** against the default 5000 ms `testTimeout`. This case spawns a child process to exercise real Node resolution, so it pays process-spawn cost — the same shape as #3662's "dist 探针" cases, which were fixed by giving them their own timeout while a sibling already had 30s.

This aborted the whole gate: `pnpm test` exited 1 with turbo reporting

```
Tasks:    26 successful, 44 total
Cached:   20 cached, 44 total
Time:     33.875s
Failed:   @objectstack/types#test
```

so **18 of 44 tasks never ran at all** — the failure is early and load-bearing, not cosmetic.

### 2. `@objectstack/dogfood` — `test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts`

```
FAIL |isolated| test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts
Error: Hook timed out in 10000ms.
 ❯ test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts:52:1
     52| beforeAll(async () => {
     53|   stack = await bootStack(showcaseStack);
     54|   token = await stack.signIn();
```

Reported as `(5 tests | 5 skipped) 10027 ms` against a 10000 ms `hookTimeout`. `bootStack` boots a full showcase stack (ObjectQL + ~45 plugins, per the boot log), which is far more than 10 s of work on a loaded box. Suite total: `Test Files 1 failed | 109 passed | 1 skipped (111)`, `Tests 775 passed | 8 skipped (783)`.

## Both pass in isolation — these are load flakes, not product defects

Re-run with nothing else on the box:

| test | isolated result | wall clock |
|---|---|---|
| `types/src/node.test.ts` run 1 | **15 passed (15)**, exit 0 | 5 s |
| `types/src/node.test.ts` run 2 | **15 passed (15)**, exit 0 | 3 s |
| `dogfood/test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts` | **5 passed (5)**, exit 0 | 29 s (27.25 s vitest) |

Note the third row: the dogfood file needs **27 s** to do its `bootStack` even unloaded. A 10 s `hookTimeout` does not cover it with any margin at all — this one looks under-budgeted independent of load, and would presumably only pass today because the boot happens to land under 10 s on faster hardware.

## Why it triggers here

`turbo.json` sets no `concurrency`, so turbo defaults to **10** parallel tasks. This container has **4 CPUs / 15 GB RAM** (`nproc=4`). Ten concurrent `test` tasks, each of which forks its own vitest workers, oversubscribes the box several times over, and the timeout-sensitive cases lose the race.

Environment:

- framework sha `e4e5c6e3c608b1b807c83a0d5b734f213eb1a1dd` (tip of `main`)
- node v22.22.2, pnpm 10.31.0, vitest 4.1.10, linux x64, 4 CPU / 15 GB
- fresh worktree, single `pnpm install`, deps prebuilt

## Reproduction

```bash
pnpm test                     # exit 1, ~34s, Failed: @objectstack/types#test
pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test   # exit 1, ~620s when run beside another build
```

then the isolated controls:

```bash
pnpm -C packages/types exec vitest run src/node.test.ts                       # 15 passed
pnpm -C packages/qa/dogfood exec vitest run test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts  # 5 passed
```

The dogfood failure above was observed while `pnpm objectui:build` was running concurrently; the `types` failure was observed with the box otherwise idle apart from turbo's own 10-way fan-out, so the default concurrency alone is enough to produce it.

## Suggested direction (not implemented here)

Following the precedent set by #3662 / #4186 / #5421 — give the two cases explicit timeouts sized to what they actually do, rather than capping repo-wide concurrency:

- `types/src/node.test.ts:178` — an explicit `testTimeout` for the subprocess-spawning cases (its siblings in the same file already run in ms; only the spawning ones are exposed).
- `dogfood/test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts:52` — a `beforeAll` timeout sized against a real measured `bootStack` (27 s unloaded here), or the suite-wide `hookTimeout` other dogfood files use. Worth checking whether sibling dogfood files already carry a larger `hookTimeout` and this one was simply missed.

Separately worth a maintainer decision: whether `turbo.json` should pin a `concurrency` proportional to available CPUs, so the whole suite stops depending on runner size. That is a broader call than this issue and is not proposed as the fix here.
